pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 📐 **Strand 3 — Geometry And Measurement**
Shape, space, measurement, position and movement — the mathematics of the world around us.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B8.3.2)
- B8.3.2.1 — Apply the Pythagoras theorem, the primary trigonometric ratios and the formula for determining the area of a circle to solve problems.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- deduce the formula A = πr² for the area of a circle and use it to solve problems
- establish Pythagoras' theorem, a² + b² = c², and use it to find missing sides
- apply Pythagoras' theorem to real-life problems and to find areas of triangles
- define sine, cosine and tangent in a right-angled triangle and use them, with angles of elevation and depression, to solve problems

pages.title: The area of a circle
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Use the relationship between the diameter and the circumference of a circle to deduce the formula for finding its area, and use this to solve problems.
Curriculum indicator B8.3.2.1.1
> 🧪 **Activity 10.1 — From circle to rectangle**
1. Draw a circle of radius 6 cm on card. Divide it into 16 equal sectors (draw diameters at every 22.5°).
2. Colour one half of the circle. Cut out the sectors.
3. Arrange them head-to-tail, alternating coloured and uncoloured, to form a shape like a rectangle (cut one end sector in half to square the ends).
4. Measure the length and width of your "rectangle". Compare them with πr and r.
[[fig:m8-f33|Figure 10.1: Sectors of a circle rearranged into a near-rectangle]]
The length of the "rectangle" is half of the circumference, [[1/2]] × 2πr = πr, and its width is the radius r.
> 🔑 **Key idea: Area of a circle** — **A = πr × r = πr²**. The area of a semicircle is [[1/2]]πr².
## ✏️ Example 10.1
Find the area of a) a circle of radius 14 cm b) a semicircle of radius 7 cm (take π = [[22/7]]).
**Solution**
a) A = [[22/7]] × 14 × 14 = 22 × 2 × 14 = **616 cm²**
b) A = [[1/2]] × [[22/7]] × 7 × 7 = [[1/2]] × 154 = **77 cm²**
## ✏️ Example 10.2
Two circles have a common centre. The small circle has radius 7 cm and the big circle has radius 14 cm. Find the area of the shaded ring between them (π = [[22/7]]).
**Solution**
[[fig:m8-f34]]
Figure 10.2: A ring (annulus)
Area = π(14²) − π(7²) = 616 − 154 = **462 cm²**

pages.title: Exercise 10.1
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 10.1** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
Take π = [[22/7]] unless told otherwise.
1. Find the area of a circle with: a) r = 21 cm b) d = 28 m c) r = 3.5 cm d) r = 10 cm (π = 3.14)
2. Find the area of a semicircle of diameter 42 cm.
3. A circular table top has a radius of 0.7 m. Varnish costs GH₵15 per m². Find the cost of varnishing the top.
4. The area of a circle is 154 cm². Find its radius and its circumference.
5. A square of side 14 cm has a circle drawn inside it, touching all four sides. Find the area of the square not covered by the circle.

pages.title: Pythagoras' theorem
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Establish the relationship between the hypotenuse c and the two other sides a and b of a right-angled triangle (a² + b² = c²) and use it to solve problems.
Curriculum indicator B8.3.2.1.2
> 🔑 **Key idea: Hypotenuse** — In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite the right angle is the **hypotenuse**. It is always the longest side.
[[fig:m8-f35|Figure 10.3: Squares on the sides of a 3-4-5 right-angled triangle]]
> 🧪 **Activity 10.2 — Squares on the sides**
1. On squared paper, draw a right-angled triangle with sides 3 units and 4 units around the right angle. Draw squares on all three sides (or construct them with compasses and ruler on plain paper).
2. Count (or measure) the area of each square: 9, 16 and 25 square units.
3. What do you notice? Repeat with a 6–8 triangle and a 5–12 triangle.
> 🔑 **Key idea: Pythagoras' theorem** — In a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse c and other sides a and b: **a² + b² = c²**. The area of the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the areas of the squares on the other two sides. Conversely, if a² + b² = c², the triangle is right-angled.
## ✏️ Example 10.3
Find the missing sides.
[[fig:m8-f36]]
Figure 10.4: Find h and AB
**Solution**
a) h is the hypotenuse: h² = 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225 ⟹ **h = 15 cm**
b) AC = 13 m is the hypotenuse: AB² = 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144 ⟹ **AB = 12 m**

pages.title: Example 10.4
pages.body:
**Indicator B8.3.2.1.3** Use Pythagoras' theorem to solve problems on right-angled triangles.
## ✏️ Example 10.4
An isosceles triangle has equal sides 6 cm long and a base of 4 cm. Find its altitude (height).
**Solution**
The altitude bisects the base, forming two right-angled triangles with hypotenuse 6 cm and base 2 cm.
h² = 6² − 2² = 36 − 4 = 32 ⟹ h = √32 ≈ **5.66 cm**
## ✏️ Example 10.5
Find the lengths indicated.
[[fig:m8-f37]]
Figure 10.5: Find x, CB and the longer length
**Solution**
a) x² = 8² + 15² = 289 ⟹ **x = 17 cm**
b) CB² = 25² − 7² = 625 − 49 = 576 ⟹ **CB = 24 cm**
c) The two right-angled triangles share the side BD. BD² = 10² − 6² = 64, so BD = 8 cm. Then the longer length CD² = 17² − 8² = 225 ⟹ **CD = 15 cm**, so the whole base AC = 6 + 15 = 21 cm.
**Indicator B8.3.2.1.4** Use Pythagoras' theorem to calculate the area of a triangle in real-life problems.
## ✏️ Example 10.6
A boat travels 2 m south and then 9 m east. How far is it from its starting point?
**Solution**
d² = 2² + 9² = 4 + 81 = 85 ⟹ d = √85 ≈ **9.22 m**
## ✏️ Example 10.7
Yeboah hangs a picture frame 15 cm wide on a wall. The wire runs from the two top corners to a nail that is 10 cm above the middle of the top edge. Find a) the length of the wire b) the area of the triangle formed by the wire and the top of the frame.
**Solution**
[[fig:m8-f38]]
Figure 10.6: Picture frame and wire
a) Each half: hypotenuse² = 7.5² + 10² = 56.25 + 100 = 156.25 ⟹ 12.5 cm. Wire = 2 × 12.5 = **25 cm**
b) Area = [[1/2]] × 15 × 10 = **75 cm²**

pages.title: Example 10.8
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 10.8
A ladder leans against a vertical wall and reaches a height of 13 m. The foot of the ladder is 6 m from the wall. Calculate the length of the ladder.
**Solution**
L² = 13² + 6² = 169 + 36 = 205 ⟹ L = √205 ≈ **14.3 m**
## ✏️ Example 10.9
The side of an equilateral triangle is 12 cm. Find a) its height b) its area c) its perimeter.
**Solution**
a) h² = 12² − 6² = 144 − 36 = 108 ⟹ h = √108 ≈ **10.39 cm**
b) Area = [[1/2]] × 12 × 10.39 ≈ **62.35 cm²**
c) Perimeter = 3 × 12 = **36 cm**
> 🎯 **BECE tip** Common Pythagorean triples: (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25) and their multiples such as (6, 8, 10). Spotting them saves time!

pages.body:

1. Find the hypotenuse: a) 6 cm and 8 cm b) 5 m and 12 m c) 1.5 cm and 2 cm
2. Find the missing side: a) hypotenuse 25 cm, one side 7 cm b) hypotenuse 10 m, one side 6 m
3. Which of these are right-angled triangles? a) 9, 12, 15 b) 4, 5, 6 c) 10, 24, 26
4. A rectangular field is 40 m by 30 m. How long is the diagonal path across it?

6. A kite string is 50 m long. The kite is directly above a point 30 m from the person holding the string. How high is the kite?

pages.title: Trigonometric ratios
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Establish the relationship between the basic trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right-angled triangles.
Curriculum indicator B8.3.2.1.5
In a right-angled triangle, name the sides relative to an acute angle θ: the **hypotenuse** (opposite the right angle), the **opposite** side (facing θ) and the **adjacent** side (next to θ, not the hypotenuse).
[[fig:m8-f39|Figure 10.7: Sides relative to the angle θ]]
> 🔑 **Key idea: Trigonometric ratios** — **sin θ =** [[opposite/hypotenuse]] **cos θ =** [[adjacent/hypotenuse]] **tan θ =** [[opposite/adjacent]]. Memory aid: **SOH CAH TOA**.
## ✏️ Example 10.10
In triangle XYZ, ∠Y = 90°, XY = 8 cm, YZ = 6 cm and XZ = 10 cm. Find sin X, cos X and tan X.
**Solution**
[[fig:m8-f40]]
Figure 10.8: Triangle XYZ
Relative to angle X: opposite = YZ = 6, adjacent = XY = 8, hypotenuse = XZ = 10.
sin X = [[6/10]] = [[3/5]] cos X = [[8/10]] = [[4/5]] tan X = [[6/8]] = [[3/4]]
## ✏️ Example 10.11
Write two trigonometric ratios of the angle θ in the right-angled triangle with sides 5, 12 and 13, where the side opposite θ is 5.
**Solution**
sin θ = [[5/13]], cos θ = [[12/13]] (and tan θ = [[5/12]])
## Angles of elevation and depression
> 🔑 **Key idea: Elevation and depression** — The **angle of elevation** is the angle between the horizontal and the line of sight when looking **up** at an object. The **angle of depression** is the angle between the horizontal and the line of sight when looking **down**. The angle of elevation from A to B equals the angle of depression from B to A (alternate angles).

pages.title: Example 10.12
pages.body:
[[fig:m8-f41|Figure 10.9: Angles of elevation and depression]]
## ✏️ Example 10.12
A hunter on top of a tower 18 m high sees a fire at an angle of depression of 30°. Find a) the distance between the fire and the hunter b) the distance of the fire from the foot of the tower. Give answers to 2 significant figures. (sin 30° = 0.5, tan 30° ≈ 0.5774)
**Solution**
[[fig:m8-f42]]
Figure 10.10: The hunter, the tower and the fire
The angle of elevation of the hunter from the fire is also 30° (alternate angles).
a) sin 30° = [[18/d]] ⟹ d = [[18/0.5]] = **36 m**
b) tan 30° = [[18/x]] ⟹ x = [[18/0.5774]] ≈ 31.2 ≈ **31 m** (check: 31.2² + 18² ≈ 36² ✓)
> 💻 **ICT corner** Use a scientific calculator in **DEG** mode: press sin 30 = to get 0.5. To find an angle from a ratio, use SHIFT sin (sin⁻¹): sin⁻¹(0.5) = 30°.

pages.title: Exercise 10.3
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 10.3** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. For a right-angled triangle with sides 7, 24 and 25, find sin, cos and tan of the angle opposite the side 7.
2. In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is 20 cm and one angle is 30°. Find the side opposite the 30° angle.
3. From a point 40 m from the foot of a tree, the angle of elevation of the top is 35°. Find the height of the tree (tan 35° ≈ 0.7002).
4. A ladder 6 m long makes an angle of 60° with the ground. How high up the wall does it reach? (sin 60° ≈ 0.8660)
5. From the top of a cliff 50 m high, the angle of depression of a boat is 25°. How far is the boat from the foot of the cliff? (tan 25° ≈ 0.4663)

pages.title: Chapter 10 summary
pages.body:
- Area of a circle A = πr²; circumference C = 2πr.
- Pythagoras: a² + b² = c² (c the hypotenuse).
- SOH CAH TOA: sin = O/H, cos = A/H, tan = O/A.
- Angle of elevation (looking up) = angle of depression (looking down) between the same two points.
